summary.title: Lisp implementations
summary.one_liner: This index page lists two blog series by Bernstein Bear on building a Lisp: one compiling Lisp to machine code, and one writing a Lisp interpreter in OCaml.
keywords: how to write a lisp interpreter step by step
how to write a lisp compiler
takeaways: The page is an index of two blog series on implementing Lisp.
The 'Compiling a Lisp' series (2020 onward) covers topics from the smallest program and integers through reader, let, if, heap allocation, and closure conversion.
The 'Writing a Lisp' series (2016-2017) covers booleans, symbols, lists, environments, closures, a metacircular evaluator, I/O, modules, and removing define.
The codecrafters build-your-own-x listing places the OCaml 'Writing a Lisp' series under building a programming language.
summary.summary: This page is a table of contents for two multi-part blog series by Bernstein Bear about implementing Lisp. The 'Compiling a Lisp' series has 12 posts dated August to October 2020, plus a closure conversion post from August 2025. The 'Writing a Lisp' series has 19 posts dated October 2016 to May 2017 and is listed in codecrafters-io/build-your-own-x as an OCaml project. The page itself contains only titles and dates, so the content of each post is not described here.
